extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, inventors, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners (practitioners involved in preparing and prosecuting U.S. patent applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for preparing, filing, and prosecuting U.S. patent applications before the USPTO (duty of disclosure, incorporation by reference, formatting of chemical/mathematical material, expungement, and inventor oath/declaration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose information material to patentability (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the filing and prosecution of a patent application has a duty of candor and good faith to disclose to the Office all information known to that individual to be material to patentability; the duty exists with respect to each pending claim until cancelled, withdrawn, or the application becomes abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no duty to submit information not material to any existing claim. The duty is deemed satisfied if all information known to be material to patentability of any claim issued in a patent was cited by the Office or submitted in the manner prescribed by §§ 1.97(b)-(d) and 1.98. No patent will be granted where fraud on the Office was practiced or the duty was violated through bad faith or intentional misconduct. The Office encourages applicants to examine prior art in counterpart foreign search reports and the closest information believed to be claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is material to patentability when it is not cumulative to information already of record or being made of record and (1) it establishes, by itself or in combination with other information, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes, or is inconsistent with, a position the applicant takes in opposing an argument of unpatentability relied on by the Office or in asserting an argument of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality requires non-cumulativeness plus either establishing unpatentability or undermining applicant positions. The formulation governs what must be disclosed under § 1.56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie case of unpatentability (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prima facie case of unpatentability is established when the information compels a conclusion that a claim is unpatentable under the preponderance of evidence burden-of-proof standard, giving each term its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, and before consideration of evidence attempting to establish patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification and evaluate whether the evidence, standing alone or combined, compels unpatentability under the preponderance standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is 'individuals associated' (duty bearers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals associated with filing or prosecution include: (1) each inventor named in the application; (2) each attorney or agent who prepares or prosecutes the application; and (3) every other person who is substantively involved in preparation or prosecution and who is associated with the inventor, the applicant, an assignee, or anyone to whom there is an obligation to assign the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals other than attorney, agent, or inventor may comply by disclosing information to the attorney/agent or inventor. (Note: AIA and pre-AIA text both provide versions; see §1.56 for applicability dates.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty in continuation-in-part (CIP) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In any continuation-in-part application, the duty includes disclosure of information known to the person to be material to patentability which became available between the filing date of the prior application and the national or PCT international filing date of the CIP application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/prosecutors must review intervening publications or other information arising after the earlier filing date and disclose material items per §1.56(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference that supplies specification/drawings for filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference made in an application data sheet in accordance with § 1.76 on filing an application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) to a previously filed application that indicates the specification and any drawings are replaced by that reference and specifies the earlier application by number, filing date, and intellectual property authority/country shall constitute the specification and any drawings of the new application for purposes of a filing date under § 1.53(b), subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to conditions and requirements of § 1.57(a); failure to comply with filing-copy/translation/fees/surcharges can result in abandonment (see following paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and requirements when relying on incorporation-by-reference to supply spec/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If relying on a previously filed application to supply the specification/drawings, the applicant must (depending on whether a correspondence address is provided) file a copy of the specification and drawings, an English translation (if required), pay required fees, and pay any surcharge within specified time periods (Office-notified period or within three months if no correspondence address) to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is abandoned under these provisions it is treated as never filed unless revived under § 1.137 and a copy of the specification/drawings is filed. Certified copy requirements and time limits (later of 4 months from filing or 16 months from the prior filing, or petition with good cause and fee) apply unless exceptions (e.g., prior-filed 111/363) exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent omission incorporation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If all or a portion of the specification or drawings is inadvertently omitted but completely contained in a prior-filed application for which a priority/benefit claim under § 1.55 or § 1.78 is present, the claim shall be considered an incorporation by reference of the prior-filed application as to the omitted portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must be amended to include the omitted portion within any Office-set time but no later than the close of prosecution (§ 1.114(b)) or abandonment. Applicant must supply a copy of the prior-filed application (except where not required), an English translation where applicable, and identify where the omitted portion is found in the prior-filed application. International-effect rules: such amendments are effective only as to the U.S.; PCT rules may apply for wider effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal wording required for incorporation by reference in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference must be set forth in the specification and must (1) express a clear intent to incorporate by reference by using the root words 'incorporat(e)' and 'reference' (e.g., 'incorporate by reference'); and (2) clearly identify the referenced patent, application, or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere reference to material does not convey intent to incorporate; the required words and a unique identification of the referenced document are necessary for an effective incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on incorporation of essential material
rubrics_metrics.description: "Essential material" may be incorporated by reference only by way of incorporation to a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that does not itself incorporate such essential material by reference. 'Essential material' is material necessary to: (1) provide a written description and enablement (35 U.S.C. 112(a)); (2) describe the claimed invention to particularly point out and distinctly claim (35 U.S.C. 112(b)); or (3) describe structure/material/acts corresponding to a claimed means or step under 35 U.S.C. 112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to incorporate essential material from non-U.S. patent sources or from documents that themselves incorporate the essential material by reference. Essential material omission can render claim support defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted sources for nonessential material incorporation; prohibited methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonessential material may be incorporated by reference to U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, foreign patents, foreign published applications, prior and concurrently filed commonly owned U.S. applications, or non-patent publications. An incorporation by reference by hyperlink or other form of browser-executable code is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit, conventional incorporation language and identify documents; do not rely on hyperlinks or browser code to incorporate content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's ability to require copy of material incorporated by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may require the applicant to supply a copy of the material incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required, the material must be accompanied by a statement that the copy supplied consists of the same material incorporated by reference in the referencing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inserting incorporated material into specification/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any insertion of material incorporated by reference into the specification or drawings must be by way of an amendment to the specification or drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an amendment must be accompanied by a statement that the material being inserted is the material previously incorporated by reference and that the amendment contains no new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of noncompliant incorporations (timing and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference that does not comply with the formal requirements is not effective unless corrected within any time period set by the Office, but in no case later than the close of prosecution (§ 1.114(b)) or abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections to satisfy the intent wording (§ 1.57(c)(1)) are permitted only if the application as filed clearly conveys an intent to incorporate; corrections to identification (§ 1.57(c)(2)) are permitted only for material sufficiently described to uniquely identify the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature/transmittal for copy-only transmittals
rubrics_metrics.description: An application transmittal letter limited to the transmittal of a copy of the specification and drawings from a previously filed application submitted under § 1.57(a) or (b) may be signed by a juristic applicant or patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits corporate or owner signature where the transmittal is solely copy delivery under § 1.57 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted content and placement of chemical and mathematical formulas/tables
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification, including the claims, may contain chemical and mathematical formulae but shall not contain drawings or flow diagrams. The description may contain tables (but the same tables should not be included in both the drawings and description). Claims may contain tables if necessary to conform to 35 U.S.C. 112 or otherwise desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow § 1.52 formatting rules; avoid duplicative placement of tables in drawings and description; use tables in claims only when required/appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirements for chemical/mathematical formulas and tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulas/tables must comply with § 1.52(a) and (b) but may be placed in landscape orientation if needed. Typewritten characters must be block (nonscript) font with capital letters at least 0.422 cm (0.166 in) high (preferably Arial, Times Roman, or Courier, 12-point), and may be no smaller than 0.21 cm (0.08 in) high (about 6-point). Provide at least 0.64 cm (0.25 in) space between complex formulas/tables and text. Formulas must maintain proper character positioning; tables should have closely spaced lines/columns while remaining highly legible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain legibility and intended meaning when formatting complex expressions; conform to USPTO type/size and spacing minima.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Large Tables' eligible for electronic ASCII submission
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Large Tables' are (1) any individual table more than 50 pages in length, or (2) multiple tables when the total pages of all tables exceed 100 pages (a table page being a paper-printed page in conformance with paragraph (b)). Such Large Tables may be submitted in electronic form as ASCII plain text via the USPTO patent electronic filing system or on a read-only optical disc, in compliance with § 1.52(e), excluding an international application during the international stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the electronic submission pathway only for tables meeting these size thresholds and follow the ASCII/plain-text rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCII plain text requirements for Large Tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Tables submitted in ASCII plain text must: maintain spatial relationships (alignment of columns/rows) to visually preserve relational information; be computer compatible (PC or Mac) and OS compatible (MS–DOS, MS-Windows, Mac OS, or Unix/Linux); include only printable characters (space allowed) and no nonprintable control characters except CRLF or LF line terminators; be named as *.txt following character restrictions and length limits; and be incorporated by reference in a separate paragraph of the specification per § 1.77(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict file formatting and naming conventions apply; ensure columns/rows are preserved in fixed-width ASCII to preserve table meaning; incorporate the file by reference in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing size and compression rules for Large Tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Tables submitted via the USPTO electronic filing system must not exceed 25 MB and file compression is not permitted. For read-only optical discs, the ASCII plain text file may be compressed using WinZip, 7-Zip, or Unix/Linux Zip, but must not be self-extracting; compressed files that do not fit on a single disc may be split and labeled per § 1.52(e)(5)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using optical discs, submit duplicate discs (Copy 1 and Copy 2) and a transmittal letter stating both discs are identical; if not identical, the Office will use Copy 1. For EFS use, ensure uncompressed file size ≤25 MB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Large Tables (electronic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendments to Large Tables in electronic ASCII plain text must include: (1) a replacement ASCII plain text file meeting requirements and labeled 'REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY'; (2) a request that the amendment be made by incorporation by reference of the replacement file in a separate paragraph of the specification identifying file name, creation date, and size in bytes; (3) a statement identifying location of all deletions/replacements/additions; and (4) a statement that the replacement file contains no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the labelling and incorporation-by-reference mechanics carefully and declare absence of new matter to avoid new-matter rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendment requirement when Large Tables present on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If a specification of an application includes Large Tables as an ASCII plain text file present on the application filing date without an incorporation by reference paragraph, the specification must be amended to contain a separate paragraph incorporating by reference the material in the ASCII plain text file in accordance with § 1.77(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add the incorporation paragraph promptly to make the ASCII file properly part of the specification record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optical disc replacement labeling rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to the information on a read-only optical disc must be by way of a replacement read-only optical disc, where the replacement disc and copy must be labeled 'COPY 1 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' and 'COPY 2 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY', respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear labeling of original and replacement discs to avoid processing errors; follow duplicate submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement of information from application file
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in an application will not be expunged except as provided in paragraph (b) of § 1.59 or §§ 41.7(a) or 42.7(a). Information forming part of the original disclosure (written specification including claims, drawings, and any preliminary amendment present on the filing date) will not be expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may petition to expunge information (excluding original-disclosure material) by filing a petition with the fee in § 1.17(g) and establishing to the Director's satisfaction that expungement is appropriate; upon grant the Office provides notice. The Office will furnish copies of an application upon request and payment of the fee in § 1.19(b) unless the application has been disposed of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath or declaration (required contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111, 363, or 385 on or after Sept. 16, 2012, the inventor (or each joint inventor) must execute an oath or declaration directed to the application. The oath/declaration must: (1) identify the inventor by legal name; (2) identify the application to which it is directed; (3) include a statement that the person believes the named inventor to be the original inventor or joint inventor of a claimed invention in the application; and (4) state that the application was made or authorized to be made by the person executing the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless an application data sheet supplies required information, the oath must also identify each inventor by legal name and provide a mailing address where the inventor customarily receives mail (and residence if different). The person executing the oath must have reviewed and understand the contents of the application, including the claims, and be aware of the duty to disclose information material to patentability per § 1.56. There is no minimum age but the signer must be competent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution and legal consequences of oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration must be executed (signed) in accordance with § 1.66 or with an acknowledgment that any willful false statement is punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 by fine or imprisonment up to five years, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatures must comply with signature rules; false statements carry criminal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing application oath/inventorship rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath/declaration is not required in a continuation application that claims the benefit of an earlier-filed application provided an appropriate oath/declaration was filed in the earlier application and a copy showing the signature or an indication of execution is submitted in the continuing application. Inventorship of a continuing application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is the inventor(s) specified in the application data sheet filed before or concurrently with the copy of the prior oath/declaration; if no ADS is filed, inventorship is as set forth in the copy of the prior oath unless accompanied by a statement under § 1.33(b) stating the names of each inventor in the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any new joint inventor named in the continuing application must provide an oath/declaration unless § 1.64 applies. Assignments may serve as oaths/declarations if they include required information and are recorded per part 3. For single-inventor applications, substitute statements under § 1.64 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA specific oath/declaration additional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA § 1.63, an oath/declaration must: be executed as required by § 1.66 or § 1.68; identify each inventor by full name (family name plus at least one given name); identify country of citizenship of each inventor; identify the application to which it is directed; state the signer has reviewed and understands the contents of the application (including claims as amended); and acknowledge the duty to disclose information material to patentability as defined in § 1.56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-AIA oath/declarations also required mailing/residence addresses (if not supplied on an ADS) and identification of relevant foreign applications for priority claims. These additional requirements apply to applications filed before the AIA applicability dates indicated in the MPEP.
